name: Anomaly of the Coronary Ostia

criteria.description: Identification of coronary ostia located outside their normal anatomical position on imaging
Coronary artery arising from an abnormal sinus of Valsalva or ectopic site
Presence of ischemic symptoms such as exertional angina or syncope unexplained by other causes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of at least both major criteria confirmed by imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on imaging modalities such as coronary angiography, CT angiography, or MRI.

pathognomonic.notes: Chest pain triggered by physical activity due to myocardial ischemia
Transient loss of consciousness due to compromised coronary blood flow

common.notes: Awareness of irregular or rapid heartbeat
Shortness of breath during physical activity

common.symptomName: Fatigue related to decreased cardiac output
searchTerms: fatigue due to low cardiac output

common.notes: ST segment changes or T wave inversions
searchTerms: electrocardiogram signs of reduced blood flow

occasional.notes: Rare but critical event due to ischemia
Reduced ability to perform physical activities

rare.notes: Heart attack occurring without typical risk factors

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; cardiac biomarkers may be elevated if ischemia or infarction occurs
imaging: Coronary angiography showing anomalous origin or course of coronary arteries
CT coronary angiography demonstrating ectopic coronary ostia
Cardiac MRI for assessment of myocardial ischemia and anatomy
genetic: No specific genetic markers identified; may be sporadic or associated with congenital heart defects
other: Electrocardiogram abnormalities consistent with myocardial ischemia or arrhythmias

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of atherosclerotic plaques on imaging
Typical risk factors such as hyperlipidemia and smoking
Intramyocardial course of coronary artery segment

redFlags: Exertional syncope or sudden loss of consciousness
Sudden cardiac arrest or unexplained sudden death
Severe exertional angina refractory to medical therapy
references: Angelini P. Coronary artery anomalies: an entity in search of an identity. Circulation. 2007;115(10):1296-1305.
Cheezum MK, Liberthson RR, Shah NR, et al. Anomalous coronary arteries: diagnosis and management. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2017;69(12):1592-1608.
